dialect.detail: Likely GnuCOBOL or similar open-source/academic COBOL; uses SCREEN SECTION with LINE/COL display, COPY with quoted filename 'LOCKLIST.ss', IS INITIAL clause, and STRING/END-STRING constructs consistent with COBOL-85 extensions
evidence: DISPLAY ... LINE LINECTR COL 3 ERASE EOL

purpose.domain_detail: User account management utility — lists locked user accounts and allows an administrator to unlock them
purpose.summary: This program reads a USER.DAT indexed file to find locked user records (RECORD-LOCK=1), writes them to a temporary indexed file TEMPUSER.DAT, then displays the list of locked users on screen with their ID and name. It is designed to allow an administrator to review and unlock user accounts.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with COPY copybook for screen layout
Indexed file I-O with DYNAMIC access mode on two files
STRING verb with multiple DELIMITED BY clauses to format user name
LINE/COL/ERASE EOL display syntax for terminal screen control
verdict.notes: The program appears to be a student project (AUTHOR: AGATHA BACANI, DATE-WRITTEN: 08 11 2018). The COPY 'LOCKLIST.ss' with a quoted filename and .ss extension suggests a GnuCOBOL screen section copybook. Some commented-out debug lines are present. The unlock functionality mentioned in the header comment does not appear to be fully implemented in the visible code.
